newsitem.title: KENYA: Closed Kenyan retail chain reopens.
newsitem.headline: Closed Kenyan retail chain reopens.

text.p: A Kenyan supermarket chain, closed on government orders over a "mad cow" scare, reopened its eight stores on Thursday after its licences were restored.
Nakumatt Holdings Ltd reopened its three stores in the capital Nairobi and five across the East African country after it received a written government reprieve on Wednesday.
Officials said workers spent part of the day clearing perishables from one Nairobi store before it was reopened.

Nakumatt stores were closed on September 19 when its trading licences were revoked on grounds it imported without proper approval 3.2 tonnes of corned beef from Britain, which has had outbreaks of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) or "mad cow" disease.
Commerce and Industry Minister Kirugi M'Mukindia told reporters on Wednesday that Nakumatt had violated Kenyan trade laws by importing beef from Britain and would remain shut.

"This beef is banned from importation to this country. If there is any indication of the worst form of capitalism, it is where a knowledgeable person, knowing the effects of the 'mad cow' disease, imports the same to be sold to people," he said.
Both Nakumatt and its supplier, British meat company John West, have stated the beef was from Brazil and packed there before being exported to Britain and re-exported to Kenya.
The commerce ministry made no comment on Thursday.
